findings.body: Both computed keys stringify a ZodType object to the same literal property name ("[object Object]"), so the second definition overwrites the first and the schema only ever requires `access_token`; the intended "expiry must be a number" validation never runs and malformed sync responses are accepted and persisted.
findings.failure_mode: Validation silently degrades to a single required field, so invalid credential-sync responses pass validation.
findings.impact: Both computed keys stringify a ZodType object to the same literal property name ("[object Object]"), so the second definition overwrites the first and the schema only ever requires `access_token`; the intended "expiry must be a number" validation never runs and malformed sync responses are accepted and persisted.
findings.root_cause: Computed object keys built from `z.string().toString()` produce identical non-descriptive strings instead of dynamic property names, which Zod cannot express.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the computed-key trick with an explicit shape plus passthrough, e.g. `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), expires_in: z.number().optional(), expiry_date: z.number().optional() }).passthrough()`, or use `z.record(z.unknown())` refinement to check the expiry field by name.
findings.title: Duplicate computed keys make minimumTokenResponseSchema validate nothing but access_token
findings.trigger: Any refresh with APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, where the self-hosted sync endpoint returns a payload with no expiry field or a non-numeric expiry.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines R8 and R10 show `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. Both computed keys evaluate to the same string ("[object Object]"), causing the second to overwrite the first. The schema effectively only validates `access_token`, breaking expiry validation.

findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a SafeParse result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), so `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` writes that wrapper object instead of the token fields; subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and the Google Calendar integration breaks for the user.
findings.failure_mode: Corrupted credential row causes subsequent credential parsing to throw.
findings.impact: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a SafeParse result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), so `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` writes that wrapper object instead of the token fields; subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and the Google Calendar integration breaks for the user.
findings.root_cause: The replacement helper returns a SafeParse wrapper while the removed `schema.parse()` returned the data itself, and the call site was not adjusted.
findings.suggested_fix: Store the parsed payload, e.g. `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema).data;` (after checking `.success`).
findings.title: Google Calendar stores the zod SafeParse result object as the credential key
findings.trigger: Any Google Calendar access-token refresh after this change.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R97 in googlecalendar/CalendarService.ts assigns `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` directly to `key`. That helper returns a SafeParseReturnType (`{ success, data }`), not the data itself. Storing this wrapper object corrupts the credential row.

raw_findings.body: The literal string "refresh_token" is persisted into the credential key, destroying the real refresh token; if credential sharing is later disabled the app can no longer refresh and the user must reconnect.

raw_findings.impact: The literal string "refresh_token" is persisted into the credential key, destroying the real refresh token; if credential sharing is later disabled the app can no longer refresh and the user must reconnect.
raw_findings.root_cause: The helper mutates parsed data with a hard-coded sentinel value that downstream callers treat as a genuine token.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Do not inject a fake value into the parsed data; leave `refresh_token` undefined and have callers preserve the previously stored refresh token when the response omits it.
raw_findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token overwrites the stored refresh token
raw_findings.trigger: Credential sharing enabled and the sync endpoint returns only an access token; e.g. Zoom's refresh path then does `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` and writes the credential back to the DB.

raw_findings.body: Those call sites immediately read `tokenInfo.data.error`, `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` or `res?.data`, which are undefined on a fetch `Response`, causing a TypeError or storing a garbage credential key instead of refreshed tokens.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Downstream property access on the wrong object shape throws or persists invalid credential data.
raw_findings.impact: Those call sites immediately read `tokenInfo.data.error`, `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` or `res?.data`, which are undefined on a fetch `Response`, causing a TypeError or storing a garbage credential key instead of refreshed tokens.
raw_findings.root_cause: A single wrapper returns the fetch Response for the sharing path while the non-sharing path returns provider-specific parsed objects, so return shapes diverge.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize the sync-endpoint result to the same shape the wrapped refreshFunction returns (e.g. `await response.json()` mapped into `{ data }` for axios/SDK callers), or give each caller a shape-specific adapter instead of returning the raw Response.

raw_findings.body: `prisma` is not imported in this file, so TypeScript compilation fails (or at runtime a ReferenceError is thrown) and the Salesforce integration cannot be used.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Build/type-check failure or runtime ReferenceError on Salesforce client creation.
raw_findings.impact: `prisma` is not imported in this file, so TypeScript compilation fails (or at runtime a ReferenceError is thrown) and the Salesforce integration cannot be used.
raw_findings.root_cause: New DB write was added without adding the corresponding prisma import.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";` to the imports of this file.
raw_findings.title: Salesforce CalendarService uses prisma without importing it
raw_findings.trigger: Any instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService (module load / booking with Salesforce connected).

raw_findings.body: The newly obtained `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` / `instance_url` are only written to the DB while the returned `jsforce.Connection` still uses `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url`, so the very request that triggered the refresh still fails with an expired token.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Refreshed token is persisted but never used for the current request.
raw_findings.impact: The newly obtained `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` / `instance_url` are only written to the DB while the returned `jsforce.Connection` still uses `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url`, so the very request that triggered the refresh still fails with an expired token.
raw_findings.root_cause: Refresh logic was inserted before the Connection construction without updating the token values passed to jsforce.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use the refreshed values when constructing the Connection, e.g. `accessToken: accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` and `instanceUrl: accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url`.
raw_findings.title: Salesforce connection still built with the stale access token after refresh
raw_findings.trigger: Salesforce credential whose stored access token has expired; getClient refreshes it and then creates the jsforce Connection.

raw_findings.body: An unconditional token-refresh HTTP round trip plus a DB write happens on every call, adding latency and risking Salesforce OAuth rate limiting / token-churn even when the stored token is still valid.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary external requests on every code path that instantiates the service.
raw_findings.impact: An unconditional token-refresh HTTP round trip plus a DB write happens on every call, adding latency and risking Salesforce OAuth rate limiting / token-churn even when the stored token is still valid.
raw_findings.root_cause: The refresh call was added inline in getClient without any token-validity precondition.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Guard the refresh with an expiry check on the stored credential (e.g. compare `issued_at`/expiry against now) and only call the token endpoint when the access token is expired or missing.
raw_findings.title: Salesforce refreshes its OAuth token on every client creation
raw_findings.trigger: Every construction of SalesforceCalendarService (each booking create/update/delete and availability lookup with Salesforce installed).

raw_findings.body: A successful refresh is treated as a failure and an HttpError with an empty message is thrown, breaking the Salesforce integration with an uninformative error.
raw_findings.evidence: if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText });
raw_findings.failure_mode: False-negative success detection aborts a valid refresh.
raw_findings.impact: A successful refresh is treated as a failure and an HttpError with an empty message is thrown, breaking the Salesforce integration with an uninformative error.
raw_findings.root_cause: Success detection relies on the optional HTTP reason phrase rather than the status code.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Check `if (!response.ok)` and include `response.status` plus the response body in the thrown error message.
raw_findings.title: Salesforce token refresh success detected via response.statusText
raw_findings.trigger: Salesforce responds over HTTP/2 or via a proxy that yields an empty `statusText`, or returns a successful non-200 status such as 201/204.

raw_findings.body: The uncaught exception surfaces as an opaque HTTP 500 with a stack trace instead of a 400 with a validation message, making integration debugging hard for self-hosters.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Client-side input errors are reported as server errors.
raw_findings.impact: The uncaught exception surfaces as an opaque HTTP 500 with a stack trace instead of a 400 with a validation message, making integration debugging hard for self-hosters.
raw_findings.root_cause: New API handler performs throwing validation without any error handling.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use `safeParse` (or wrap the handler body in try/catch) and return `res.status(400).json({ message: ... })` on validation/decryption failure.
raw_findings.title: Webhook body validation throws an unhandled ZodError
raw_findings.trigger: A correctly authenticated caller posts a body missing `userId`/`appSlug`/`keys` or with wrong types (also applies to a malformed encrypted `keys` value reaching `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` below).

raw_findings.body: A constant whose name implies a boolean flag actually carries the encryption key secret, so any logging/serialization of the constant leaks the key, and typed consumers expecting `boolean` get a string.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Flag constant holds secret material and has the wrong type.
raw_findings.impact: A constant whose name implies a boolean flag actually carries the encryption key secret, so any logging/serialization of the constant leaks the key, and typed consumers expecting `boolean` get a string.
raw_findings.root_cause: Logical AND of two env strings is exported directly without boolean coercion.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the expression in a boolean coercion: `export const APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED = !!(process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY);`
raw_findings.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string, not a boolean
raw_findings.trigger: Both env vars set: the exported constant evaluates to the raw value of CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY (typed `string | undefined`).

raw_findings.body: Breaks the file's sorting convention, making future merges and duplicate detection in this long list error-prone.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Convention violation degrades maintainability of the env allow-list.
raw_findings.impact: Breaks the file's sorting convention, making future merges and duplicate detection in this long list error-prone.
raw_findings.root_cause: New env key appended at an arbitrary position in a sorted list.
raw_findings.title: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET inserted out of alphabetical order in turbo globalEnv
raw_findings.trigger: Reading or editing the `globalEnv` array, which is otherwise alphabetically sorted (the new entry sits after "CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY").

raw_findings.failure_mode: Duplicated constant can drift from config.json.
raw_findings.impact: An unrelated regression in this PR: the slug is no longer single-sourced from `appConfig.slug`, so a slug change silently breaks the OAuth redirect, and the template literal now has no interpolation (lint noise).
raw_findings.root_cause: Config-derived value replaced by a hardcoded string unrelated to the credential-sync feature.
raw_findings.title: Zoho Bigin redirect URI hardcodes the slug instead of using appConfig.slug
raw_findings.trigger: Reviewing/refactoring the Zoho Bigin app slug; the callback path is now duplicated instead of derived from config.json.

finding.body: An unconditional token-refresh HTTP round trip plus a DB write happens on every call, adding latency and risking Salesforce OAuth rate limiting / token-churn even when the stored token is still valid.
finding.failure_mode: Unnecessary external requests on every code path that instantiates the service.
finding.impact: An unconditional token-refresh HTTP round trip plus a DB write happens on every call, adding latency and risking Salesforce OAuth rate limiting / token-churn even when the stored token is still valid.
finding.root_cause: The refresh call was added inline in getClient without any token-validity precondition.
finding.suggested_fix: Guard the refresh with an expiry check on the stored credential (e.g. compare `issued_at`/expiry against now) and only call the token endpoint when the access token is expired or missing.

finding.verifier_reason: Patch lines R75-R99 show the token refresh fetch is executed unconditionally inside `getClient` with no expiry check. Every instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService triggers a refresh round-trip, adding latency and risking rate limits.

finding.trigger: Both env vars set: the exported constant evaluates to the raw value of CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY (typed `string | undefined`).

validated_findings.body: Both computed keys stringify a ZodType object to the same literal property name ("[object Object]"), so the second definition overwrites the first and the schema only ever requires `access_token`; the intended "expiry must be a number" validation never runs and malformed sync responses are accepted and persisted.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Validation silently degrades to a single required field, so invalid credential-sync responses pass validation.
validated_findings.impact: Both computed keys stringify a ZodType object to the same literal property name ("[object Object]"), so the second definition overwrites the first and the schema only ever requires `access_token`; the intended "expiry must be a number" validation never runs and malformed sync responses are accepted and persisted.
validated_findings.root_cause: Computed object keys built from `z.string().toString()` produce identical non-descriptive strings instead of dynamic property names, which Zod cannot express.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the computed-key trick with an explicit shape plus passthrough, e.g. `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), expires_in: z.number().optional(), expiry_date: z.number().optional() }).passthrough()`, or use `z.record(z.unknown())` refinement to check the expiry field by name.
validated_findings.title: Duplicate computed keys make minimumTokenResponseSchema validate nothing but access_token
validated_findings.trigger: Any refresh with APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, where the self-hosted sync endpoint returns a payload with no expiry field or a non-numeric expiry.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines R8 and R10 show `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. Both computed keys evaluate to the same string ("[object Object]"), causing the second to overwrite the first. The schema effectively only validates `access_token`, breaking expiry validation.

validated_findings.body: The literal string "refresh_token" is persisted into the credential key, destroying the real refresh token; if credential sharing is later disabled the app can no longer refresh and the user must reconnect.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Persisted credential state is corrupted with a sentinel string.
validated_findings.impact: The literal string "refresh_token" is persisted into the credential key, destroying the real refresh token; if credential sharing is later disabled the app can no longer refresh and the user must reconnect.
validated_findings.root_cause: The helper mutates parsed data with a hard-coded sentinel value that downstream callers treat as a genuine token.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Do not inject a fake value into the parsed data; leave `refresh_token` undefined and have callers preserve the previously stored refresh token when the response omits it.
validated_findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token overwrites the stored refresh token
validated_findings.trigger: Credential sharing enabled and the sync endpoint returns only an access token; e.g. Zoom's refresh path then does `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` and writes the credential back to the DB.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R26 shows `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token";` – a literal string is injected when the field is missing. Downstream code persists this, corrupting the stored credential if credential sharing is later disabled.

validated_findings.body: Those call sites immediately read `tokenInfo.data.error`, `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` or `res?.data`, which are undefined on a fetch `Response`, causing a TypeError or storing a garbage credential key instead of refreshed tokens.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Downstream property access on the wrong object shape throws or persists invalid credential data.
validated_findings.impact: Those call sites immediately read `tokenInfo.data.error`, `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` or `res?.data`, which are undefined on a fetch `Response`, causing a TypeError or storing a garbage credential key instead of refreshed tokens.

validated_findings.title: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response to callers expecting axios/SDK objects
validated_findings.trigger: Credential sharing enabled (CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set) and a Zoho Bigin / Zoho CRM / HubSpot / Google credential is refreshed.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines R8-R15 in refreshOAuthTokens.ts return the raw fetch `Response` when credential sharing is enabled, while the else branch returns the result of `refreshFunction()`. Callers like Zoho Bigin (line 96 `tokenInfo.data.error`) expect an axios-style object, causing TypeError or garbage credential writes.

validated_findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a SafeParse result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), so `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` writes that wrapper object instead of the token fields; subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and the Google Calendar integration breaks for the user.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Corrupted credential row causes subsequent credential parsing to throw.
validated_findings.impact: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a SafeParse result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), so `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` writes that wrapper object instead of the token fields; subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and the Google Calendar integration breaks for the user.
validated_findings.root_cause: The replacement helper returns a SafeParse wrapper while the removed `schema.parse()` returned the data itself, and the call site was not adjusted.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Store the parsed payload, e.g. `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema).data;` (after checking `.success`).
validated_findings.title: Google Calendar stores the zod SafeParse result object as the credential key
validated_findings.trigger: Any Google Calendar access-token refresh after this change.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R97 in googlecalendar/CalendarService.ts assigns `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` directly to `key`. That helper returns a SafeParseReturnType (`{ success, data }`), not the data itself. Storing this wrapper object corrupts the credential row.
